title: What each fused kernel computes, joined with what it costs (B=65 vs B=75)
method: --xla_dump_to already wrote the post-optimisation HLO; opstep never read it. This joins four sources per kernel: the HLO (fusion kind, the opcodes inside the fused computation, the root instruction, the output shape), the thunk sequence (grid/block), the profiler trace (us and launch count), and the HLO metadata op_name, which carries the JAX source path.

fusion_kinds_reference.note: XLA's fusion strategy is not described in official documentation; the enum comments in the source are the authoritative description.
fusion_kinds_reference.kLoop: The primary node is the root of the fused computation, but, unlike in input fusion, we prescribe a specific implementation for codegen. Rather than generating code that looks like the code we'd emit for an unfused version of the primary/root node, we emit code that generates ONE ELEMENT OF THE ROOT AT A TIME. (verbatim) -- this per-element loop is what the vectorisation width widens, so the v2(B)+v2(L)>=2 rule acts on kLoop fusions.
fusion_kinds_reference.kInput: The primary node is the root of the fused instruction. (verbatim) -- used for reductions, where an implementation 'might emit something more sophisticated'.
fusion_kinds_reference.kOutput: The primary node is not the root of the fused instruction; requires an operand buffer able to alias the output buffer.
fusion_kinds_reference.kCustom: Custom category for backend-specific fusions that don't fit into the above patterns. (verbatim)

headline_finding.claim: Only a fifth of the runtime is the Metropolis physics. A third is just moving neighbours.

the_kCustom_finding.why_it_matters: This is the kernel that carried 67.8% of the gap in opstep_65_75.json, and it is kCustom. kLoop fusions emit 'one element of the root at a time', which fixes their grid at ceil(elements/width/128) and makes them proportional to B. kCustom uses a backend-specific emitter under no such obligation, which is why this is the only kernel of the 43 whose blocks-per-replica is not constant.
the_kCustom_finding.refines_earlier_claim: I earlier called the two sides 'the same operations'. Precisely: identical PTX load/store signature (ld_scalar=69, ld_v4=0, st=16) and identical op tally except ONE negate present at B=65 and absent at B=75, i.e. 70 vs 69 ops. Same operation up to a folded sign, not byte-identical.

limits: 38 of the 40 fusion kernels were matched to their HLO fusion (36 exact, 2 by stripping one trailing index). The 3 remaining unmatched entries are memory copies, not fusions.

Two real fusion kernels went unmatched: loop_log_plus_one_maximum_fusion_1 / loop_maximum_negate_fusion_1 (11.5% of runtime) and loop_add_slice_fusion_1 (1.4%). GPU kernel names are built by the emitter from the fused computation's opcodes, so they do not always equal the HLO instruction name. Their role in the table is inferred from the kernel name alone and is labelled as such.
The role grouping is my attribution, grounded in the JAX source path (op_name) and the opcode composition, not a label XLA emits.
Totals differ about 1% from opstep_65_75.json (8,931.5 vs 9,027.7 us/replica at B=65): run-to-run variation, single run each.
Measured at 3600 sweeps. The 5.2% gap here is 0.6% at production, so this dissects the short-schedule artefact; see prodstep_65_75.json.
